front: Chain-rule factorisation of a text's probability
back: $p(x_1..x_T)=\prod_t p(x_t\mid x_{<t})$; an identity, the model parametrises each factor.
$\mathcal L=-\frac1N\sum_t\ln p_\theta(x_t\mid x_{<t})$: cross-entropy of the true next token, averaged over all positions.

front: Gradient of softmax cross-entropy w.r.t. the logits
back: $p-\text{onehot}(y)$: probabilities minus the one-hot truth. Shape $(V)$ per position.
$\exp(\text{cross-entropy})$: the effective number of equally likely tokens the model hesitates between. Uniform model: $V$. Perfect: 1.

front: When can two perplexities be compared?
back: Only for the same tokeniser and the same text; otherwise the units being predicted differ.
The inputs shifted one position to the right; a window of length $T$ yields $T$ examples.
Position $t$ may only attend to positions $\le t$, so a pass over a window trains all next-token predictions without cheating.
Reuse the token-embedding matrix as the output head. For GPT-2 small it removes about 38.6M parameters (163M -> 124M).
Sample from $\operatorname{softmax}(z/T)$. $T\to0$: greedy; $T=1$: model distribution; $T\to\infty$: uniform.
Keep the $k$ most probable tokens, renormalise. Cuts the tail but $k$ is fixed regardless of model confidence.
Keep the smallest set of top tokens whose cumulative probability $\ge p$, renormalise. The set size adapts to confidence.
Temperature, then top-k, then top-p, then draw from the renormalised distribution.

front: Why is counting the optimum for a bigram model?
back: For each context row, minimising cross-entropy over the simplex gives the empirical frequencies (Gibbs inequality). Gradient descent reaches the same point iteratively.

front: Why do plain n-gram tables not scale?
back: They need $V^n$ cells and most contexts are never seen; neural models share parameters across similar contexts.
